question.text: Which of the following is a CORRECT principle of valuation as stated in the chapter for Cat I/II AIF portfolio marks?

answer.text: Value of a business is fixed at IPO and rarely changes thereafter
Liquidity has no impact on private-market valuations
Only book value matters; cash flows are irrelevant
Valuation is time-specific and depends on future cash flows, with market forces dictating the rate of return; liquidity affects value

explanation.text: The Logic: Per PDF Section 11.8: (1) 'Valuation is time specific. The value of a business changes every day...' (2) 'Value depends on future cash flows.' (3) 'Certain market forces dictate the rate of return...' (4) 'Liquidity affects the value of a company. With the increase in the liquidity ... its value increases.' All four principles must be held together. The Trap: Other options contradict at least one of the four PDF-stated principles. This is a direct recall question testing whether you internalised the chapter's stated principles. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests the same. CFA L2 and IPEV list similar axiomatic valuation principles. Manager's Pro-Tip: Use these four principles as the opening slide of your fund's Valuation Policy Manual. They are the compass by which every individual asset mark is justified to auditors and LPs.
